step1_analysis.description: A 3-stage ring oscillator where the first stage includes a tail transistor used as a switch. Injecting a high-frequency signal into this switch modulates the stage delay, allowing the oscillator to lock to a subharmonic (typically divide-by-2) of the injection frequency.

paper_reference.title: A 44-W 4.3-GHz Injection-Locked Frequency Divider With 2.3-GHz Locking Range

operating_frequency.description: The output frequency of the divider when locked to the input signal.

sky130_expected.calculation: With L=0.5um, node capacitance is ~50fF. At VDD=1.8V and BIAS=0.8V, PMOS current is ~84uA. Stage delay ~ 50fF * 0.9V / 84uA = 0.53ns. Free-running frequency ~ 1 / (6 * 0.53ns) = 314 MHz. Locked frequency will be half of the injection frequency.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Significantly lower than the paper due to the large channel length (L=0.5um) specified in the netlist parameters.

power_consumption.description: Total DC power consumed by the circuit from the supply.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Higher than the paper's minimum power because we are operating at VDD=1.8V instead of 0.7V, and the PMOS loads are biased for higher current to ensure oscillation with L=0.5um.

division_ratio.description: Ratio of the input injection frequency to the output frequency.

sky130_expected.reasoning: The circuit is designed to operate as a divide-by-2 ILFD.

output_amplitude.description: Peak-to-peak voltage swing of the output signal.

sky130_expected.calculation: Swings from near GND to near VDD depending on the PMOS load strength.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Standard full-swing or near full-swing operation for a ring oscillator.

step3_testbench.description: Transient analysis to verify injection locking, measure output frequency, division ratio, and power consumption.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Injection-Locked Frequency Divider Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u
.param W_xm3=5u L_xm3=0.5u
.param W_xm4=5u L_xm4=0.5u
.param W_xm5=5u L_xm5=0.5u
.param W_xm6=5u L_xm6=0.5u
.param W_xm7=5u L_xm7=0.5u
.param W_xm8=5u L_xm8=0.5u

XM1 N2 OUT N1 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM2 BUF_OUT OUT GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}
XM3 N1 IN GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm3} w={W_xm3}
XM4 N2 BIAS VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm4} w={W_xm4}
XM5 OUT N0 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm5} w={W_xm5}
XM6 N0 N2 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm6} w={W_xm6}
XM7 OUT BIAS VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm7} w={W_xm7}
XM8 N0 BIAS VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm8} w={W_xm8}

VVDD VDD 0 1.8
VBIAS BIAS 0 0.8
VIN IN 0 SIN(0.9 0.9 600MEG 0 0)
Rbuf BUF_OUT VDD 10k

.ic v(N0)=0 v(N2)=1.8 v(OUT)=0

.control
tran 10p 100n

* Measure input frequency
meas tran t_in_period trig v(in) val=0.9 rise=20 targ v(in) val=0.9 rise=21
let f_in = 1 / t_in_period

* Measure output frequency
meas tran t_out_period trig v(out) val=0.9 rise=10 targ v(out) val=0.9 rise=11
let f_out = 1 / t_out_period

* Calculate division ratio
let div_ratio = f_in / f_out
print f_in f_out div_ratio

* Measure power consumption
meas tran i_vdd avg i(VVDD) from=50n to=100n
let power = -i_vdd * 1.8
print power

* Measure output amplitude
meas tran v_max max v(out) from=50n to=100n
meas tran v_min min v(out) from=50n to=100n
let v_pp = v_max - v_min
print v_pp

quit
.endc
